entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Afranius was an ancient Roman comic poet who lived at the beginning of the 1st century BC.

Born into a wealthy family in Rome, Lucius Afranius was educated under the tutelage of prominent scholars and eventually became known for his witty and satirical poetry. His works were widely performed during festivals like the 'Dissertatio' and 'Ludi Plebisculari' events, entertaining masses with stories of love, politics, and everyday life.

Afranius's notable contributions include 'Jocasta', a tragicomedy adaptation of Sophocles' 'Oedipus Rex', which was first performed in 89 BCE at the Theater of Pompey. This work showcased Afranius's innovative style, blending elements of comedy and tragedy to create a unique narrative voice.

The legacy of Lucius Afranius can be seen in the enduring popularity of Roman satire, with his works influencing later writers like Plautus and Terence. His impact on Western literature is undeniable, demonstrating the power of art to shape societal attitudes towards politics, morality, and human relationships.
